 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the order of dismissal of his claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as per order dated 01.09.2016 in MVC No.663/2013 passed by the Second Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chikmangaluru (In short 'the Tribunal')..

entities.text: Second Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chikmangaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 01.09.2013 at 9:00.pm. near Rampura Circle, Chikkamagaluru,
while the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA.18/U-5174 as pillion rider, Appe goods auto bearing Reg.No.KA-18/8210 dashed against the motorcycle due to which the petitioner sustained injuries, he was treated at M.G Hospital Chikkamagaluru and Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital.

entities.text: Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After taking the treatment, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the respondent.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties by impugned NC:
2024:KHC:32997 judgment and award dismissed the claim petition with cost.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Vinod Gowda., learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri. H.N.M.Prasad,
learned counsel for respondent No.1-Owner and Sri. B.C.Shivanne Gowda., learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
5.

It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that though the accident took place on 01.09.2013, rider of the motorcycle, carried the injured to the Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital.

entities.text: Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After return home, he has filed the complaint to the police on 03.09.2013, there is a valid explanation for delay in filing the complaint.
When the accident is admitted, the burden is upon the respondent to prove that the accident occurred on account of negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
The order of dismissal is erroneous.
No compensation is assessed by the Tribunal.
Hence, requests for remand of the matter for assessment of the compensation by accepting the accident in question.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the owner of the vehicle has contended that in the written statement there is a specific statement made that the petitioner was the rider of the NC:
2024:KHC:32997 motorcycle and not the complainant.
The Appe goods auto was not dashed against the motor cycle, the motorcycle, which was coming behind the Appe goods auto hit on the hind portion.
For this reason, the petitioner has sustained head injuries.
The averments made in the prosecution papers are contrary to the pleadings of the petitioner.

The Tribunal has rightly Sri Kantharaja vs Sri Surendra on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166675832/
2 appreciated the said aspect and came to the conclusion that the accident is not proved and dismissed the claim petition and support the impugned judgment.

entities.text: Sri Kantharaja vs Sri Surendra on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that accident took place on 01.09.2013, whereas the complaint was filed three days later.
The material on record is able to explain complaint was the rider of the motorcycle.
No MLC was registered at Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital nor at Government Hospital, Chikkamagaluru.

entities.text: Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hospital records did not point out the accident.

If, the rider was not suffered any injuries and having taken the injurer to the Government Hospital, Chikkamagaluru, MLC register extract is not placed before the Court to explain that the accident occurred as proposed by the petitioner.
The prosecution papers speak differently than that of what is NC: 2024:KHC:32997 pleaded in Paragraph No.22 of the claim petition.
The Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to arguments addressed on behalf of both the sides and perused the material on record.
9. The material on record point out that on 01.09.2013 at 9:00.pm, there was an accident involving the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA.18/U-5174 and Appe goods auto bearing Reg.No.KA-18/8210.

In the accident, the petitioner has no doubt suffered fracture of left patella, fracture of left maxilla,
fracture of zygoma, fracture of left orbit, open fracture of lateral condyle of left femur with communited chip.
On 02.09.2013, the petitioner was taken to Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital, where he was treated as inpatient, till 11.09.2013.

entities.text: Shivamoga Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The wound certificate issued by the District Hospital, Chikkamagaluru refers to the history of accident as "RTA bike hit to Auto-Appe standing at 9:30.pm".

Where as the NC:
2024:KHC:32997 charge sheet marked as per Ex.P.4 point out that the accident took place, while the Appe goods auto was going ahead all of a sudden without signal took turn towards Adishakthi Nagar due to which the motorcycle came and dashed on the back left side of the Appe goods auto.
10. The written statement of respondent No.1 clearly attribute that the petitioner was the rider of the motorcycle.
The evidence of the petitioner would not deny the said aspect in his evidence.
What has been pleaded in Paragraph No.22 of the claim petition is identically placed in the form of affidavit evidence.
The medical records speaks that the bike hit against the standing Appe goods auto.
The owner of the vehicles stated that the bike came and hit on the hind portion of the Appe goods auto.
The charge sheet speaks that the Ape goods auto took sudden turn facilitating the motor cycle rider to hit on the back left side of the Ape goods auto.

11. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it is seen that the Tribunal did not point out these lacunae and not properly appreciated the evidence whether the accident took place due to headon collusion between the motorcycle and the Appe goods auto?, whether the motorcycle hit the standing Appe NC: 2024:KHC:32997 goods auto?, whether the Appe goods auto while going, took sudden turn facilitating the motorist to hit against the Appe goods auto?.

The Tribunal also not considered the point, who was the rider of the motorcycle at the time of the accident whether the petitioner as Sri Kantharaja vs Sri Surendra on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166675832/
3 pleaded by respondent No.1 or the complainant as stated in the complaint and the charge sheet.

entities.text: Sri Kantharaja vs Sri Surendra on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. The matter requires detailed enquiry for which, both the parties are required to place proper evidence before the Tribunal, so as to come to a just conclusion about how the accident has occurred.
If the petitioner is proved to be the pillion rider then his entitlement for compensation has to be considered by the Tribunal.
So also the Tribunal did not consider the aspect of contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
That apart, the owner, rider and insurer of the motorcycle are not made as parties to the claim petition.
In a case of this nature, they are also necessary parties.
13. Hence, the appeal merits consideration for remand.

In the result, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:32997 ORDER i) The appeal is hereby allowed.
ii) The impugned judgement and award is set aside.
iii) The matter is remanded to the Tribunal to the stage of further evidence of the petitioner.
iv) The Tribunal is directed to allow both the parties to lead further evidence and to decide the case, in the light of the observations made supra in accordance with law.

v) Without further notice, parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 12.09.2024.
SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE PHM CT: BHK Sri Kantharaja vs Sri Surendra on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166675832/
